correctness.rationale: For each scalar quadratic, the Polyak ratio is exactly \(1/(2ca_i)\), so the capped update is \(x^+=(1-r_i)x+r_ib_i\) with \(r_i=\min\{q,a_i\gamma_b\}\) and \(0<r_i\le1\). Synchronous coupling is uniformly contractive, giving a unique stationary law. Its first- and centered second-moment fixed-point equations give the displayed mean and variance exactly. Factoring \(\gamma_b\) from \(r_i\) yields the clipped-curvature surrogate and all phase boundaries. Independent simulation of a mixed-cap example matched the exact stationary moments, and the piecewise formulas were checked algebraically.

value.rationale: The cap is a practically meaningful algorithmic parameter, and outside interpolation it changes the stationary target rather than merely limiting step magnitude. The exact clipped-curvature target, bias-variance decomposition, and phase thresholds give a motivated diagnostic benchmark for SPSmax and are more than a routine restatement of its known loose-cap failure.
